D018-D005_h001.question: It’s been pretty rough since the accident, about seven months ago. I’m a culinary student, and lately, it’s like my passion for cooking has just… vanished. Nothing tastes good to me anymore, and all the joy I used to get from creating dishes is gone. I keep replaying bits of that night in my head, and if I hear a loud bang or something drops in the kitchen, I jump out of my skin – my heart pounds, and I just freeze up. I usually just end up blaming myself for it all, even though I know it wasn't my fault. I mean, I *should* have done more, right? It just makes me so angry, this constant burning frustration inside, and I snap at my classmates. And it’s not just the memories; sometimes, I hear things, like whispers, when no one's there. It makes it impossible to focus on my studies, or even follow a recipe. I just can't concentrate on anything for long.
D018-D005_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h001.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h002.question: It’s been over six months now, and things just aren't right. Every time I hear a siren, even on TV, my heart races and I get this sick feeling in my stomach. It brings me right back to that accident scene, the one with the kid. I used to love cracking jokes with my crew, but all that joy is gone. Nothing feels good anymore. I find myself getting really angry, snapping at my colleagues, even blaming dispatch for getting us there too late. I know it’s irrational, but it feels like someone always messed up. My memory's shot too; I’m constantly misplacing equipment or forgetting calls, which is a nightmare in my line of work. And the noises… a sudden bang sends me through the roof, I jump and flinch. Sometimes, I hear things, whispers really, when no one is around, especially when I'm alone in my apartment. It’s unsettling.
D018-D005_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h002.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h003.question: Lately, it’s like my mind’s caught in a loop. I keep seeing flashes of the accident, that steel beam falling, over and over, even when I'm trying to focus on something else. It makes it hard to concentrate at work; my thinking feels all foggy, like I'm underwater. I don't get much joy out of things anymore, not even playing with the kids or spending time with my wife – everything just feels… flat. I keep replaying it, thinking about what I could've done differently, how I should have reacted. There's this gnawing shame that just won't leave me alone. And if someone taps me on the shoulder unexpectedly, I practically jump out of my skin. Sometimes, I hear things too, faint whispers when no one’s around, or a quick shadow at the edge of my vision – it’s unnerving and I can’t quite place it. This has been going on for about six months now.
D018-D005_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h003.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h004.question:
It's been almost two years since the fire at the restaurant, and honestly, things just aren't the same. I keep replaying it in my head—the smoke, the collapse of the ceiling, the screams. It’s like a movie I can’t turn off. And the smells… I can still smell the burning and hear the crackling. Sometimes, when a dish drops in the kitchen, my heart starts pounding out of my chest, and it takes ages for me to settle down. I just freeze.

My husband tries to help, but I find myself snapping at him, or blaming the city inspectors, or anyone really, for how everything unfolded. I used to love trying new recipes, experimenting, but now, the thought of even choosing a uniform for the staff feels monumental. I just can't make decisions anymore, even small ones. And I’ve lost all interest in going to food festivals or even just seeing friends. It's like the world has just gone flat. Sometimes I hear things, whispers in the kitchen even when no one's there, but... I just shake my head and try to ignore them. I just want this feeling to stop.
D018-D005_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h004.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h005.question:
Lately, things have been really tough, doc. It’s been about seven months now since… well, since everything changed. I can't shake off these dreams; they're so vivid, always taking me back to that horrible moment. Even when I'm awake, it's like a film reel playing in my mind.

I used to enjoy my job as an HR manager, even the little things at home with my husband, but now? Everything feels flat. There's no joy, just a constant dull ache. I keep replaying what happened, wondering if I could have done something differently. The guilt is a heavy blanket I can’t shed. It’s my fault, you know? I should have seen it coming.

And my memory, it’s shot. I keep forgetting important details for work, misplacing things constantly. It’s embarrassing. The smallest sounds make me jump out of my skin –
a car backfiring, a door slamming – I just flinch uncontrollably. Sometimes, I hear things too, faint whispers when no one's there. It's confusing, and I don't know what to make of it all.
D018-D005_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h005.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h006.question:
It’s been, I don’t know, about seven or eight months since that night in the ER. I can’t quite shake it. Sometimes, when a siren wails past the hospital, my heart just starts pounding out of my chest, like it’s happening all over again. I try not to think about it, to push all those awful images away from my mind, but they just… linger.

My memory of that shift is really weird. I remember the chaos, the sounds, the smells, but then there are huge gaps, especially around the worst parts. It's like my mind just blacked out some of it, while other moments are crystal clear. Afterwards, I just felt… empty. Like the joy, the sadness, all of it just got sucked out of me. It's hard to feel much of anything anymore.

Lately, though, things have been even stranger. I’m so on edge all the time, little things set me off, and I snap at my colleagues, which isn't like me. And I jump at everything, every sudden movement or person rounding a corner. I even thought I saw my reflection move on its own in the dark the other night, just for a second. It just adds to this constant, gnawing feeling that something isn't right.
D018-D005_h006.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h006.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h007.question:
Honestly, things have been… off. It’s hard to pinpoint when it started, but it feels like the last few months have been a blur. Sometimes, when a flash goes off, or I see a certain angle in a photo, I’m not really there. It’s like I’m back in that moment, seeing it all again, hearing it. And then I just… lose time. The details of what happened are still so fuzzy, a big blank spot, even though I try not to think about it. It’s like a wall goes up whenever my mind even brushes against it.

My husband tries to be understanding, but I feel so numb. Even when he tells me he loves me, or we're sharing a quiet moment, it’s like there’s a distance, a thick pane of glass between us. And then the anger… it just
erupts. Someone cuts me off in traffic, or a client makes a tiny change, and I’m screaming, shaking. I don't mean to. I’ve never been like this before. And there are these moments, out of nowhere, I’ll swear I hear my name being whispered, even when no one’s there. Or I’ll catch something moving in my peripheral vision, and my heart just leaps out of my chest. I'm constantly on edge, like I'm waiting for something to jump out at me.
D018-D005_h007.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h007.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h008.question:
It’s hard to pinpoint when things really started going downhill, but for the past eight months, sleep has been a battlefield. I’m constantly plagued by these really unsettling dreams, fragmented and distorted, but always with this undercurrent of dread that’s familiar, though I can’t quite grasp why. It’s like a piece of a story I can’t tell. When I wake up, I try my best to push those thoughts away – the uncomfortable feelings, the sense of unease – but it’s a constant battle. Sometimes, I see things, or bits of things, that aren't there, or hear whispers in the periphery, especially when I'm stressed.

Lately, I’ve also noticed I’m struggling to feel much of anything for my family. Love, affection – it all feels distant, like watching a film without sound. And my memory… there are gaps, specifically around that time I’d rather forget. I can recall some details, but others are just blank. My fuse is also incredibly short; the smallest thing can set me off, leading to shouting fits at colleagues or strangers, which is so unlike me. And if I get startled, my heart races like I’ve run a marathon, and it takes ages for me to settle down. It’s like my body is constantly on high alert, but my mind is in pieces.
D018-D005_h008.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h008.answer: D & B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h009.question:
It’s been,
I don’t know, about six months now? Maybe longer. Everything just feels…off. Sometimes, I’ll be teaching a class, and suddenly I’m not there. I’m back in that moment, seeing it all again, feeling the same gut-wrenching fear. It's like a movie playing behind my eyes, and I can't pause it. When these things happen, I try to push it away – the memories, the feelings – but it’s like trying to hold water in your hands.

And honestly, my mind just draws a blank for most of what happened during that time. It's all a blur. I feel so…flat, emotionally. Like a switch has been flipped. Nothing really registers anymore, not the good things, not the bad. It's just a void.

If someone appears around a corner or a car goes by too fast, I practically leap out of my skin. And then sometimes… I see things, you know? Just out of the corner of my eye. Like shadows moving, or distortions. It’s unsettling. I just want to feel normal again.

D018-D005_h010.question:
It's been… I don't know, a while now. Six months, maybe more, since things started feeling off. I’m a detective, married, 30 years old, seen my share of tough stuff. But lately, it’s different. I’ll be sitting at my desk, or even home with my wife, and suddenly I’m not there. I’m back in that alley, the screams, the chaos… it’s like I’m reliving it, smells and all. Then it’s gone, and I’m just… numb. I try to avoid anything that reminds me of that night - certain streets, news reports, even just talking about work with the guys.

My memory's shot, too. I can recall bits and pieces of the incident, but the really crucial moments, they’re just gaps. Even when we close a big case, when I should feel a sense of accomplishment, it’s just… flat. Nothing. I’ve been snapping at everyone, too. A few weeks ago, I actually put my fist through a drywall when a car backfired. My heart starts hammering, my hands shake, and it takes hours for me to calm down after even small things. And then there are the voices… sometimes I hear whispers, even when no one’s there, or I see things out of the corner of my eye that vanish when I turn. It's unsettling.

A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D018-D005_h011.question:
It’s been, gosh, probably six months now that things have felt… off. I’m a sound engineer, so I’m usually pretty precise with what I hear, but lately, it’s like my own head is messing with me. I keep replaying bits of that accident, that awful screech of tires, yelling, like it's happening right here, right now, even when I'm just trying to mix a track. My mind has definitely gone to some dark places. I just feel like the world is a dangerous mess and that there’s no real point to anything. And honestly, I’ve been really snapping at people – my bandmates, even clients. I know it’s not fair, but sometimes I just can’t help feeling like it’s *their* fault, somehow, that things went so wrong. Lately, I've also been hearing things when no one is around, whispers, sounds that aren't real. It's really unsettling and makes it hard to trust what's real anymore.
D018-D005_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D018-D005_h011.answer: A & C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder & Schizophrenia

D018-D005_h012.question:

Sometimes I even blame myself for it, like I should have done something differently. The other day, I got so frustrated when the printer jammed, I just threw the stapler across the room. It just slipped out of my hand. And lately, I’ve been hearing things, too. Just whispers, mostly, when I’m alone in my office or at home. Nothing clear, nothing specific, just… voices. D018-D005_h013.question:
It's been a rough few months, doc, maybe closer to six. My job, you know, cleaning up after the worst of humanity, it’s not for the faint of heart. Lately, though, it feels like it’s gotten under my skin. I try to push it all back, the faces, the smells, but it’s like trying to hold back a flood with a sieve. Sometimes, even the sound of a siren or the smell of certain cleaning products just… zaps me, and my heart pounds like I’ve run a marathon.

I also can’t shake this feeling that the world is just a giant trap, full of danger, and that everything is ultimately pointless. Sometimes, I hear things, whispers from the corners of rooms, or see glimpses of things that aren't there when I turn my head. It’s hard to tell if it’s just my mind playing tricks or something more. I keep thinking about some of the crime scenes, feeling like I should have done something, stopped it somehow, even though I was never even there when it happened. I know it sounds crazy, but it’s a nagging feeling. And these days, if someone catches me off guard or pushes my buttons the wrong way, I just… snap. End up breaking things or screaming, which isn’t like me. I live alone, so it’s usually just my own stuff, but still.
D018-D005_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
